subject: Treasuries' Worst Quarter Since '94
body_text:
Good morning! Here's the latest in trending:Frontier model: Google (GOOGL) reveals Gemini 4 Argon amid internal doubts over performance.Economy watch: Fed hike bets ease as inflation not as hot as expected. Private sector hiring picks up.Renovation probe: Fed watchdog clears Jay Powell of wrongdoing, but Trump wants him gone.

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Frontier model: Google ( GOOGL ) reveals Gemini 4 Argon amid internal doubts over performance .

 Economy watch:  Fed hike bets ease as inflation not as hot as expected. Private sector hiring picks up .

 Renovation probe:  Fed watchdog clears Jay Powell of wrongdoing, but Trump wants him gone .

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Higher for longer 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
The U.S. bond market just completed its worst quarter this century, with the Treasury selloff pushing yields to two-decade highs as traders brace for higher-for-longer interest rates. Other factors include strong economic data combined, ongoing concerns about energy-driven inflation and mounting fiscal debt.

 Fresh highs:  The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield ( US10Y ) went up 87.1 basis points over the September quarter, LSEG data showed. That's the sharpest quarterly rise since 1994.  US10Y rose as much as 6 bps to 5.34% early today, notching its highest level since 2002, just a day after it surpassed its previous 2007 peak. The 30-year Treasury yield ( US30Y ) was up 3 bps at 5.67%, also a 24-year high. "What is striking, however, is how little of this has spilled over into broader risk assets," Principal Financial Group pointed out. "Despite a significant repricing in the bond market, the S&P 500 ( SP500 ) remains close to record highs, while credit spreads have remained relatively tight. Together, both suggest investors continue to view higher yields as a reflection of economic strength rather than deteriorating conditions."

 Zoom in: While recent inflation data and still-resilient growth indicate that the Federal Reserve may wait till December to raise interest rates again, markets are pricing in at least three hikes by mid-2027. There are also concerns over the U.S. fiscal outlook as well as heavy government and corporate issuance, particularly for the costly AI buildout. "For now, the bond market appears unconvinced that slower growth, lower inflation, or fiscal restraint are close at hand," Seeking Alpha analyst James Picerno noted on Thursday. "Until one of those narratives gains traction, Treasury yields may continue marching higher, testing not only the economy's resilience but also investors' willingness to keep pricing in a best-case scenario centered on improving economic activity," he added.  Nobody Wants To Catch The Falling Knife As The Bond Market Tanks 

 Zoom out: There's another factor pressuring the bond market – the unwinding of the Japanese yen ( USD:JPY ) carry trade. "The major central banks' quantitative easing policies rigged global bond markets," market strategist Ed Yardeni  noted, explaining that this era kept "bond vigilantes"—investors who protest fiscal recklessness by selling bonds and driving up yields—at bay. "Now, the chickens have come home to roost ." Carry traders are now being forced to sell the government bonds they purchased worldwide. Without the Bank of Japan's artificially cheap money subsidizing global debt, governments that accumulated massive deficits from the great financial crisis through the pandemic are facing the true cost of their borrowing. "Now, we may be witnessing the Revenge of the Bond Vigilantes," Yardeni added.

 Broadcom to lend Anthropic ( ANTHRO ) ≤ $42B to lease chips .

Oracle ( ORCL ): No major damage  from flooding  at Project Jupiter .

 Constellation , Amazon ( AMZN ) ink 20-year nuclear power deal .

Ford ( F ) slips as F-150 supplier setback to impact Q3 sales .

Netflix ( NFLX ) co-CEO: We're not growing as fast as I want us to .

Fed finalizes changes to bank stress tests to curb capital volatility .

Pentagon launches Project Meridian to identify future warfare tech .

Trump touts South Korea's $200B investment plan in energy projects .

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Today's Markets
 
 
 
 In Asia, Japan +3.3% . Hong Kong +0.4% . China closed. India -0.8% .
 In Europe, at midday, London -1.3% . Paris -0.9% . Frankfurt -0.3% .
 Futures at 6:30, Dow -0.1% . S&P +0.2% . Nasdaq +0.6% . Crude +1.5% to $91.73. Gold +0.2% to $4,194.30. Bitcoin -0.2% to $83,687.
 Ten-year Treasury Yield +2 bps to 5.31%.
